en: The Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Holy Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Great Teacher of the Dharma, the Purple-Robed Śramaṇa Subject [of the Tang], from Nālandā Monastery in Magadha, Central India.
Translated by Fātian by Imperial Decree. Thus have I heard.
At one time, the World-Honored One was staying on the summit of Mount Nandana, not far from the abode of the rishis in a celestial palace, together with a great assembly of five hundred bhikṣus.
Furthermore, there was an assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
all these bodhisattvas were destined to attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment after only one more birth.
Their names were as follows:
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra,
and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Anantapuspa.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantakusuma,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganagañja,
and five hundred such Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas were present together with him.
At that time, the World-Honored One and the various bodhisattvas saw,
by a river in a forest at the foot of that mountain,
two bhikṣus who were naked, stretching out their arms, wailing and weeping. Thereupon, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganagañja—
He immediately rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder,
knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms in reverence,
and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One."
"For what cause and for what reason are those two bhikṣus by the side of the Gaṅgā River naked, stretching out their hands, crying out and weeping?
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, saying:
Those two bhikṣus were afflicted by disease and possessed by bhūtas; therefore, they were naked, wailing and weeping.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha—
He addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One, how may such illnesses be eliminated?
How may such obstacles (vighna) be dispelled?
At that time, the World-Honored One, by means of his supernormal powers, summoned all the Buddhas.
At that time, six Tathāgatas appeared in the sky in order to bear witness to the Dharma of the seventh World-Honored One,
the Tathāgata Śākyamuni. Then, the Tathāgata Vipaśyin...
For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings,
eliminating diseases, and expelling bhūtas,
I joyfully proclaim this dhāraṇī, saying:

Namo buddhāya | Namo dharmāya | Namaḥ saṃghāya | Oṃ cara cara hiri hiri hirāya | Namo jñānamūrtaye | Namo nāthāya | Svāhā. At that time, the Tathāgata Vipaśyin, having spoken this vidyā-mantra, [passed away].
He addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, saying:
"If there be anyone who receives, maintains, recites, and makes offerings to this dhāraṇī,
you should know that such a person shall be free from the suffering of disease and shall not be harmed by weapons."
Water cannot wash them away and poison cannot harm them;
they shall not suffer untimely death, nor shall they have any ailment regarding food or drink.
They will attain the power of hearing and retaining, and their lifespan will be long and far-reaching.
At all times, the Buddhas will protect and keep one in mind.
Furthermore, if one has deafness, by reciting a mantra over oil seven times and dripping it into the ear,
the affliction will naturally dissipate.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śikhin,
desiring to benefit all sentient beings,
sought to eliminate diseases and dispel bhūtas.
He joyfully proclaimed the dhāraṇī, saying:

*Namo buddhāya | namo dharmāya | namaḥ saṃghāya | oṃ | paṭa paṭa | paṭa paṭaya | sarvabhūtānām | kṣiṇi kṣire | paraviniyanām | svāhā*. At that time, the Tathāgata Śikhin, having spoken this vidyā, [became silent].
He addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, saying:
"This Great Dhāraṇī of the Heart-Seal has been proclaimed together by hundreds of thousands of koṭis of countless Buddhas."
If there are sentient beings who, throughout the six periods of day and night, remember and uphold this Heart Dharani of mine,
their illnesses will be eliminated, malevolent spirits will stay far away, evil dreams will be dispelled, and they will forever be free from premature death.
Calamities shall not invade them, and poisons shall not harm them.
They will dream of the Tathāgata entering the realm of the Buddha.
Furthermore, [they shall be freed from] diseases such as wind-disorders, jaundice, and afflictions caused by *kumārabhṛta* spirits.
Tie a blue thread cord with this mantra and wear it upon the body;
recite the mantra by the ear at all times, and may all [afflictions] be extinguished.
At that time, the Tathāgata Viśvabhū [spoke].
Desiring to benefit all sentient beings, to eliminate diseases, and to dispel *bhūtas*,
he joyfully proclaimed this *dhāraṇī*:
*Namo buddhāya | namo dharmāya | namaḥ saṃghāya | oṃ kara kara | karaka ra | kuruṣāna kuru | sarvagraheṣu svāhā.* At that time, the Tathāgata Viśvabhū, having spoken this vidyā-mantra, [passed away].
He addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, saying:
"Listen attentively now to this dhāraṇī.
It has been proclaimed together by the Tathāgatas of the Bhadrakalpa and all Buddhas of the three times. If there are those who receive, uphold, read, recite, and make offerings to this dhāraṇī..."
It should be known that such a person cannot be harmed by weapons or stung by poison;
they shall be free from all diseases and cannot be swept away by water;
nor shall they meet an untimely death, as their past karma will be eliminated.
If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās,
they should first bathe and stand before the World-Honored One;
by reciting and maintaining this vidyā-mantra eight hundred times, no diseases or afflictions whatsoever shall be able to harm them.
One shall attain long life and exhaust all afflictions;
one shall obtain vast treasuries of wealth and grain;
and all evil beings shall be struck with fear.
By contemplating and reciting this dhāraṇī, fears are eliminated and one obtains what is cherished.
If there is any dispute or debate,
by tying knots with white thread while reciting the dhāraṇī, all shall be reconciled.
If one suffers from eye pain, one should make a cord from the milk-tree (*kṣīravṛkṣa*), recite the dhāraṇī, and tie it around the neck; thus one will immediately be cured.
Furthermore, if one sees military forces arrayed against one another...
Take honey, curd, ghee, and *apāmārga*;
perform *homa* by reciting [the mantra] once and casting [an offering] into the fire each time,
until eight thousand repetitions are completed.
All the military forces shall mutually maintain their battle arrays and enjoy long lives.
For the sake of seeking peace and security, the king and his ministers shall perform *homa* offerings of curd,
honey, and rice pollen into the fire eight thousand times.
In all places, body and mind shall experience happiness.
Whether for oneself or for all sentient beings,
it eliminates the afflictions of the aggregates, calamities, karmic obstacles, and inauspicious signs.
Recite the mantra over white milk-tree fuel and sesame seeds,
performing eight thousand *homa* offerings in the fire;
all calamities and misfortunes will then be immediately eliminated.
Furthermore, if there is a person who wishes to achieve mastery over all vidyā-mantras,

they should take one hundred *nāraṅga* flowers, *bhallātaka*, *gośīrṣa-candana*, *śvetotpala*, *karkaṇḍu*, *mūṣṭaka*, *indravāruṇī*, coral, and *jāti*— these medicinal substances— and place them together in an auspicious flask.
Insert branches of the Bodhi tree and *sumana* flowers into the mouth of the auspicious vase (*bhadraghaṭa*) and place it before the World-Honored One.
On the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight, recite the *dhāraṇī* before the World-Honored One for one day and one night.
When it has been recited eight hundred times, the *siddhi* will be accomplished.
At that time, the Tathāgata Karkuṭaṇa,
desiring to benefit all sentient beings, [spoke thus].
To eliminate diseases and expel bhūtas,
he joyfully proclaimed the dhāraṇī, saying:
*Namo buddhāya, namo dharmāya, namo...*
Namaḥ saṃghāya | Namaḥ kalyāṇacakṣuṣe tathāgatāya | Arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya | Oṃ kaṭa kaṭa kaṭa kaṭa kiṭi ||
Cici cici (11) cici cici (12) namo sarvatathāgatādhipatirājāya samayasambhavāya (13–16).
*Svāhā*. At that time, after the Tathāgata Karkuṭaṇa had spoken this vidyā,
he addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, saying:
Listen attentively now!
This Great Dharani of the Heart-Seal has been proclaimed by as many Buddhas,
World-Honored Ones, as there are sands in the Ganges River.
If there are those who uphold, make offerings to, hear, or rejoice in this dhāraṇī,
you should know that such persons will obtain the power of hearing and retaining, be far removed from illness, have no afflictions regarding food and drink, and be liberated from all bonds.
At a later time or a later period, if there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas,
or upāsikās who offer incense, flowers, and unguents to the Triple Gem,
bathe the World-Honored One, and with a resolute mind recite this dhāraṇī;
By reciting it eight hundred times, one attains the supernormal power of recollecting past lives;
for seven births one dwells in the heavens as a son of the gods,
and upon descending to the human realm, one becomes a wheel-turning monarch.
If one recites according to the conditions rather than strictly following the ritual rules,
one will always be reborn among humans;
upon the end of life as a human, one will be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
If one empowers various kinds of food and drink seven times,
all illnesses will be entirely eliminated.
If one seeks to pacify and remove all demonic influences and eight thousand obstacles, [the same applies].
First, one should bathe and recite this vidyā seven times.
If one suffers from malignant sores, one should recite over the sore seven times.
If one suffers from boils or swellings, one should empower a copper needle.
If one recites the mantra while applying the needle, the ailment will be immediately cured.
In all cases of conflict and strife, if one recites this vidyā seven times,
the discord will be immediately dispersed.
If one recites this vidyā while bound by all fetters,
completing it seven times, one will immediately attain liberation and an increase in wealth and treasures.
One should maintain the recitation of this dhāraṇī constantly and without interruption.
Regarding all obstacles and difficulties (*vighna-vināyaka*):
by reciting this dhāraṇī seventeen times, one will immediately be freed from them.
If a person wishes to know the matters sought by the mind:
In a pure place, such as before a Buddhist stūpa,
having solemnly prepared a maṇḍala and burned aloeswood incense,
one should recite this vidyā-mantra eight thousand times.
Lying with his head toward the east, he saw the Tathāgata in a dream;
he beheld all things—the length of their lifespans, their merits and demerits, and their superior or inferior qualities.
At that time, the Tathāgata Kanakamuni [appeared].
For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings,
eliminating diseases, and dispelling bhūtas,
he joyfully proclaimed the dhāraṇī, saying:
Namo buddhāya | Namo dharmāya | Namaḥ saṃghāya | Namaḥ kānakāmune | Tathāgatāya | Rahaṭe | Samyaksambuddhāya | Oṃ | Sara sara | Sara sara | Siri siri | Si... ||1||
RISIRI (12) SIRĀYA (13) DHAMA DHAMA (14) DHAMA DHAMA (15) TĀRE TĀRE (16) TĀRE TĀRE (17) TĀRAYA (18) NAMO NAMAḤ (19) KĀNAKAMUNAYE (20) TATHĀGATĀYA ARHATE (21) SAMYAKSAMBUDDHĀYA (22) SVĀHĀ (23)
HŪṂ HŪṂ (twenty-three). At that time, after the Tathāgata Kāñcanamuni had spoken this vidyā, he addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, saying:
If there are those who receive, uphold, read, and recite this dhāraṇī, and constantly make offerings to it,
you should know that for such persons, all weapons, swords, water, and fire [shall not cause harm].
One will not be harmed by fearsome heterodox teachings, incantations, or various poisons, nor shall one meet an untimely death.
All karmic obstructions created in previous lives will be completely eliminated through recitation and mindfulness performed during the three periods of the day.
Furthermore, for scabies, leprosy, abdominal tumors, and malignant swellings,
one should grind sweet flag (*achyranthes aspera*) into a powder, mix it with honey to form pills,
and perform *homa* offerings in the fire eight thousand times.
Furthermore, for malarial fevers that recur every one, two, three, or four days,
one should empower *jāti* and *sumana* flowers and wear them on the body.
If one suffers from deafness, one should recite the mantra near the ear.
Furthermore, if there are ailments of wind-disorder, epilepsy,
or *kaṭaka* spirits, by consecrating Buddha-flowers and wearing them upon the body,
may all such diseases be eliminated.
May you always behold the Tathāgata, enjoying wealth, honor, and long life;
at all times, may all Buddhas protect and keep you in mind.
At that time, the Tathāgata Kāśyapa...
For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings,
eliminating diseases, and dispelling bhūtas,
I joyfully proclaim this dhāraṇī, saying:

Namo buddhāya | Namo dharmāya | Namaḥ saṃghāya | Oṃ | Hara hara | Hara hara | Ha ha | Namaḥ kṣāntipāya | Tathāgatāya | Arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya | Abhiṣiñcatu māṃ mantrapadaiḥ | Svāhā. At that time, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Kāśyapa, having spoken this vidyā-mantra, [the assembly was filled with joy].
He addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha,
saying: "If there be anyone who receives, maintains, reads, recites, or makes offerings to this dhāraṇī,
you should know that all their karmic obstructions will be entirely eliminated, and they shall be sustained by all Buddhas at all times."
One should distance oneself from unwholesome dharmas and abide securely in wholesome dharmas.
Furthermore, if there is a person afflicted with the disease of white leprosy,
they should empower Buddha-flowers eight thousand times.
If one has a chronic fever, one should consecrate Buddha-flowers eight thousand times.
If one has recently contracted an illness,
one should consecrate Buddha-flowers eight thousand times and wear them upon the body.
May all such things be eradicated at all times.
Furthermore, if a woman experiences difficulty in childbirth while pregnant,
one should empower *buddhapuṣpa* oil by reciting mantras over it, then apply it by rubbing it on [the body].
If one has skin diseases or wind-induced sores, one should empower Buddha-flowers and ghee, then fry them together and apply the mixture to the lesions.
Furthermore, for abscesses, swellings, or various types of hemorrhoids and fistulas,
one should empower Buddha-flowers and fine honey, then apply them together to the sores.
Furthermore, for those suffering from malarial fevers occurring every day, every second day, every third day, or every fourth day;
for all diseases caused by ghosts, such as those involving the consumption of odors or flowers;
or for those with epilepsy—one should empower Buddha-flowers and wear them upon the body.
By the empowerment of the power of clarity regarding such illnesses as these,
may they all be extinguished at all times.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni—
For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings,
eliminating diseases, and dispelling bhūtas,
he spoke this Heart-Seal Dhāraṇī, saying:

Namo buddhāya | Namo dharmāya | Namaḥ saṃghāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ | Kumi kumi | Mahākumi | Tre tre | Mahātre | Cale | Namo buddhāya | Namo dharmāya | Namaḥ saṃghāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ | Kumi kumi | Mahākumi | Tre tre | Mahātre | Cale |

*Kiḷi kiḷi* (28), *mahākiḷi* (29), *ciri ciri* (30), *mahāciri* (31),
*svāhā* (32). At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, having spoken this vidyā, [remained silent].
He addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, saying: "Gaganagañja,
you should know that if there is anyone who receives, upholds, recites, and makes offerings to this dhāraṇī,
that person shall be free from physical illness."
They shall not be harmed by swords or staves, nor swept away or drowned by water;
they shall not undergo suffering or meet with untimely death.
Ākāśagarbha, you should now know that this dhāraṇī possesses great majestic power.
It can eliminate diseases and eliminate all poisons;
it can eliminate inauspiciousness and all fears.
Neither those bhūtas nor their hosts will be able to cause harm.
If one recites "Bhutana Bhutana," the hosts [of obstructors] will be unable to cause harm;
thus, these various hosts will each give rise to a mind of loving-kindness and ensure their peace and security at all times.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, the Tathāgata has already spoken of this great dhāraṇī which benefits sentient beings and accomplishes peace and security."
I shall now also proclaim the *dhāraṇī* for the benefit of sentient beings, which purifies the *dharmadhātu*, brings about accomplishment, and bestows peace.
It is as follows: *tadyathā | cale cale mahācale | ture ture mahāture | jvale jvale mahājvale | heḍe heḍe mahāheḍe | svāhā*. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha...
Having spoken this illumination, he further said:
"If one wishes to accomplish supramundane and extraordinary merit,
one should receive and uphold this dhāraṇī."
All weapons, fetters, diseases, or afflictions,
as well as the obstructions of black clouds and the poisons of *vīra* creepers, shall be unable to cause harm.
Furthermore, if there should be the disease known as *kākuṇḍanī-ādimṛtyu-sthāra*,
may it all be eliminated through the power of this vidyā and its protection.
At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken this Dharma, [remained silent].
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha and the entire great assembly,
having heard what the Buddha had spoken,
received and upheld it with single-minded devotion, and joyfully practiced it accordingly.
The Sutra of the Dhāraṇī of the Holy Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha
